title: Mutating values behind an Rc handle
prompt: Why does the compiler prevent direct mutation of data stored inside an `Rc` pointer?
answer: `Rc` provides shared ownership across multiple handles without runtime borrow tracking. Allowing direct mutation through one `Rc` handle would invalidate references held by other handles. To mutate data safely behind shared ownership, pair `Rc` with `RefCell` or use `Rc::make_mut`.
